message.content:
I’m sorry—I don’t have direct access to real‑time clocks or external services, so I can’t tell you the exact minute right now.  

If you’d like to find out yourself:

| Tool / Method | How to use |
|---------------|------------|
| **Smartphone/Computer** | Most devices show the correct local time automatically once their time zone is set to “New York” (Eastern Time). |
| **Web search** | Typing “current time in New York” into Google will display the up‑to‑second UTC+/- offset. |
| **Command line** | On Linux/macOS: `TZ=America/New_York date` – this prints the current time in NYC’s time zone. |
| **Python example** | ```python\nimport pytz, datetime\nny_tz = pytz.timezone('America/New_York')\nprint(datetime.datetime.now(ny_tz))\n``` |

> ⚠️ Remember that New York observes Daylight Saving Time, so its offset from UTC switches between −5 h (Standard) and −4 h (DST).

Let me know if you’d like help writing a script or setting up a widget!
